title: Ticket Queue
statement:
Run a ticket line with your language's standard queue. People join at the back, and the person at the front is served first.

The first line is the number of commands `n`. Each of the next `n` lines is a command: `join NAME` puts NAME at the back of the line, and `serve` removes the person at the front. A name is one word with no spaces, and the same name can join more than once. For each `serve`, print the name of the person served on its own line, or `empty` when nobody is waiting. There is at least one `serve` command.

Input:

```text
5
join Ana
join Ben
serve
join Cal
serve
```

Expected output:

```text
Ana
Ben
```

tests.stdin:
5
join Ana
join Ben
serve
join Cal
serve

6
join Max
join Max
join Zoe
serve
serve
serve

hints: A queue is first in, first out: add at the back, remove from the front.
Check whether the queue is empty before you remove anyone.
